messages:
Alyssa: Hey folks, hitting weird behavior in staging TF workspace during an import. terraform plan now shows a provider mismatch and wants to replace our aws_db_subnet_group. I imported via CI and the state seems to be tied to the wrong provider alias. Anyone seen provider alias mapping flip after importing from a different runner?

Mike: Can you paste the provider blocks and the exact import command you ran?

Alyssa: Sure — provider config (simplified):
```terraform
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-west-2"
}
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "us-east-1"
  region = "us-east-1"
}
module "db" {
  source = "../modules/db"
  providers = {
    aws = aws.us-east-1
  }
}
```
Import command I ran from CI: `terraform import -var-file=staging.tfvars module.db.aws_db_subnet_group.private sg-0123abcd` — CI runner is in us-west-2 so I suspect the import attached the default provider instead of the aliased one.

Devon: Yep, that makes sense. Terraform associates resources in state with the provider address that was used by the process doing the import. If the CI run used the default aws provider, the state will reference that provider (no alias).

Alyssa: Ok. Is there a way to reassign the provider on the state without destroying the resource?

Mike: Use `terraform state replace-provider`. Example: `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws:us-east-1'`. Test it on a copy of state first.

Sasha: Also run `terraform state show module.db.aws_db_subnet_group.private` to confirm which provider address is recorded right now.

Alyssa: Ran `state show` — it shows `provider = provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]` (no alias). I tried `replace-provider` locally but got an error complaining the provider address doesn't match.

Devon: Use `terraform providers` and `terraform state pull` to inspect exact addresses. Addresses in state can be quoted differently depending on TF version. You might need to target `provider["aws"]` vs the full registry address.

Alyssa: I tried running on a copy: `terraform state replace-provider -state=copy.tfstate 'provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]' 'provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws:us-east-1"]'` — that succeeded on the copy and `terraform plan -state=copy.tfstate` shows no replacement now.

ops-bot: Reminder: always take a state backup & run these ops in a locked environment. :warning:

Mike: Nice. After replace-provider, run `terraform plan -refresh=true` in CI and confirm no diff. Also add a check to CI to fail if `terraform providers` outputs mismatched addresses so this doesn't regress.

Sasha: Can you paste the exact replace command you used so others can reproduce?

Alyssa: Final command I used: `terraform state replace-provider -state=copy.tfstate 'provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]' 'provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws:us-east-1"]'` — validated plan looks clean. Will run on staging with lock and backup shortly. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
